newsitem.title: GERMANY: Govt report sees German '97 growth at 2.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Govt report sees German '97 growth at 2.5 pct.

text.p: Germany's economy is expected to grow by 2.5 percent this year, up from 1.4 percent in 1996, according to an annual government economic report, details of which were obtained by Reuters on Tuesday.
Other key forecasts from the report include inflation at 1.5 percent, an unemployment rate of 11 percent and growth in industrial investment of 1.5 percent.

The report, which is still being drafted and is not due to be published for a week, showed Bonn sticking to the growth forecast underpinning Finance Minister Theo Waigel's bid to cut state borrowing and qualify for European monetary union.

Some independent economists expect gross domestic product (GDP) to grow more slowly than the official view, pressuring tax revenues and making it harder to cut the budget deficit below the Maastricht Treaty's ceiling of three percent of GDP.
Figures from the report, compiled by the Economics Ministry, showed both eastern and western Germany would grow at the same pace.

No figure was given for the expected number of jobless, but an 11-percent rate indicates a further rise in unemployment from a forecast in October by Germany's panel of six institutes which saw unemployment at 10.4 percent, or four million.
German unemployment rose above 4.1 million in December, and officials and economists expected that will climb to a new post-war record of around 4.5 million this winter.
